messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: New App: shiny + d3 + GeneNet/ENA = Reconstruct Gene Regulatory Networks
parts:
I created a new application using shiny, d3, and a couple of R packages to infer genetic networks. The application is currently hosted on Glimmer at:
http://glimmer.rstudio.com/qbrc/grn/

I'm using Shiny/Glimmer to handle all web traffic, and ENA to wrap GeneNet to do the actual network inference (more methods could easily be added later). I used D3's Force Layout to provide some interactive network visualization -- I don't know that it's really the most practical way to view the data, but it's some fun eye-candy.

I had stumbled through a few un-documented features of Shiny (app-specific `www` directories, JS to handle custom Shiny outputs, fileInput() for uploading data, etc.) -- if you find yourself in the same boat, all my source is available on Github here if anyone's interested.

As the warning in the UI says, I've had a lot of difficulty using the `fileInput()` function to allow users to upload their own data. When running the app locally, it seems that Firefox and Chrome both work. But when running the app remotely (as on Glimmer), I haven't had consistent success with any single browser, so you may be better off uploading your data elsewhere and then pasting the URL in.

Hope you find it (or the code) useful!

Jeff

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: New App: shiny + d3 + GeneNet/ENA = Reconstruct Gene Regulatory Networks
parts:
Hi Germán,

I'm glad you enjoy the app.

Regarding the d3 integration, first, I'd recommend taking a look at http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#building-outputs . They have a pretty good introduction to what it would take to get a custom widget in Shiny to work.

I apologize for the sloppiness of the code (my first stab at this and I should really go back and clean things up now that I have a better understanding of how to put JS code into Shiny), but the relevant portion is here: https://github.com/trestletech/shiny-sandbox/blob/master/grn/graph.js

Basically, the JS function defined in that file's `renderValue` field dictate what my app will do with the incoming JSON data returned by the Shiny server. In this case, I'm going to build a d3-based object out of it and show in an SVG element.

Hope that helps!
Jeff
